visual.footnote: PKCE mandatory · tokens verified against public JWKS

standards.sentence: We implement the specs exactly: PKCE on every authorization code, rotating refresh tokens, revocable signed sessions, published signing keys.

features.title: Identity plumbing, handled.
features.intro: Everything below is live today unless marked otherwise — each card names the mechanism, because that is what you are actually buying.

items.title: Universal login
items.body: A hosted sign-in flow your users get redirected to — email one-time codes, no passwords to store, no login UI to maintain.

items.title: Session management
items.body: Sessions are signed RS256 JWTs in http-only cookies, with idle and absolute expiry, server-side revocation, and per-environment keys.

items.title: Token security
items.body: Authorization codes always travel with PKCE. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and a replayed token revokes its whole family.

items.title: Audit ledger
items.body: Every security event lands in a hash-chained audit log per environment — tampering breaks the chain, and the chain recomputes from genesis.

items.title: Abuse controls
items.body: Fixed-window rate limits on code delivery, verification attempts, and token issuance. Lockouts consume outstanding codes; copy stays neutral.

items.title: Management API
items.body: One API surface for applications, users, sessions, and logs at /api/v2, driven by scoped machine tokens.

privacy.title: Your tenants' data stays yours.
privacy.intro: Auth is identity infrastructure — we process exactly what authentication requires and publish every detail. No ad trackers, no data sale, no model training on tenant data.
processed: Account email, to deliver one-time codes
Authentication events with technical metadata, kept for security and audit
Transient abuse-prevention counters that expire on their own
Credentials and cryptographic keys stored only in protected form
never: Sell, rent, or share personal data — ever, for any purpose
Load third-party trackers or ad pixels on auth surfaces
Train models on tenant or end-user data
Keep data after you close your account, beyond legal minimums

quickstart.title: Three requests to a working login.
quickstart.intro: No proprietary protocol, no vendor lock-in — everything below is stock OAuth 2.1 and OIDC against our live endpoints.

steps.title: Discover our endpoints
steps.body: Your app reads standard OIDC discovery — no SDK required, any language works.

steps.title: Send users to /authorize with PKCE
steps.body: Create a code challenge, redirect the browser, we handle the hosted login and email code.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
steps.body: Verify the id_token against our public JWKS, keep the refresh token, call userinfo when you need claims.

pricing.title: Priced by users, not by locks.
pricing.intro: Early-access pricing. A monthly active user is a user who authenticated at least once that month; you are never billed for stored-but-idle accounts.

features: Audit ledger and auth event logs
MFA, passkeys, and enterprise SSO as they ship

pricing.note: Billing is not yet automated — early-access tenants are invoiced manually and can leave anytime.
